the-logo-three.title: From the Logo
the-logo-three.prompt: The shot from the logo, overtime, 2016. One figure, alone. A slight guard in a dark navy sleeveless jersey with a large gold 30 has just released a jump shot from the centre-court logo on his OWN half of the floor, one stride before the half-court line, seen from behind and slightly above so the entire empty far half of the court stretches away in front of him. Both arms are still raised in the follow-through. The ball is a burning comet with a long golden trail arcing high across a black sky toward a tiny glowing rim at the far end, 38 feet away. The half-court line crosses the floor just in front of his feet; the court's lines run to the horizon like a runway and fade into darkness. Nobody else on the floor. Navy and gold on black.

the-bounce.title: The Bounce
the-bounce.prompt: Game 7 at the buzzer, 2019. Only two figures. A forward in a black jersey with a white 2 is crouched low on his heels in the right baseline corner, inches inside the sideline, both hands on his knees, staring up. A tall defender in a white jersey with a red 21, who just closed out on him, is still in the air beside him with one arm up. The rim stands at the top of the frame with the ball balanced on the front of its iron, frozen at the top of its fourth bounce, glowing like the only light in a dark arena. A shot clock above the backboard reads 0.0. The floor below them is a sliver of hardwood; everything else is black and the crowd a wall of faint red. Black, white and red.

the-dagger.title: The Dagger
the-dagger.prompt: Game 7 of the 2016 Finals, 53 seconds left. Only two figures. A guard in a black jersey with a gold 2 is at the top of his jump on the right wing, well outside the three-point arc, releasing a step-back three with the ball just off his fingertips above his head. The defender in a white jersey with a gold 30 is directly in front of him, a half step too late, lunging with his right arm stretched up toward the ball, off balance. Seen from the baseline at floor level. The three-point arc glows under the shooter's feet; the ball's path is a thin red line toward a rim at the left edge. Behind them, instead of a crowd, a solid wall of yellow light. Black, wine red and gold on yellow.

the-shrug.title: The Shrug
the-shrug.look: Smoke and warm rim light, a black arena.
the-shrug.prompt: The player is a Black man in a white jersey with red trim and white shorts, jogging back up the floor toward the viewer after the sixth three, just past the broadcast table. The shrug exactly as it happened: both elbows bent and held out from his body, forearms level, both palms open and turned up at chest height, shoulders lifted, head turned to his right toward the broadcast table at the right edge of the frame, a faint perplexed half-smile, mouth slightly open, face partly lit and partly in shadow - the face of no one in particular. Nobody else on the floor. No clock, no scoreboard.
concepts: Six basketballs hang in an arc in the black above him, each burning like a small sun and trailing fire, their light falling on his shoulders through the drifting smoke.

Seen from the broadcast table's side of the floor so he looks almost toward the viewer. Behind him, drawn in thin lines of gold light across the dark arena, six arcs rise from six spots beyond the three-point line and fall into one distant rim, the paths of the six threes still hanging in the air.

A wide shot from high in the rafters: the arena a vast dark bowl, the player tiny at mid-court with his palms up, and six white spotlight beams stabbing down from the roof and converging on him, the only light in the building.

Behind him the rim and its net are enormous, filling the top of the frame, the net still swinging, and six balls lie scattered on the hardwood under it where they fell, each one glowing faintly. Smoke along the floor.

the-flu-game.title: The Flu Game
the-flu-game.prompt: The flu game, Game 5 of the 1997 Finals. Only two figures. Two teammates in red road jerseys walking off the floor together toward the viewer. The one on the right, with a white 23, is slumped and spent, head hanging, legs barely under him. The one on the left, with a white 33, holds him up with an arm wrapped around his shoulders. Behind them the arena is a dark, feverish blur, and the hardwood runs back into fog. A sickly green cast in every shadow, the two red jerseys the only saturated colour. Red on black with green shadows.

the-block.title: The Block
the-block.prompt: The chase-down block, Game 7 of the 2016 Finals. Only two figures. A guard in a white jersey with a gold 9 is in the air under the rim on the right side, at the end of a layup, the ball just leaving his hand toward the glass. A forward in a black jersey with a gold 23 has arrived from behind at full stretch, flying in from the left, and pins the ball flat against the backboard with his right hand, inches from the rim. Seen from behind the baseline, slightly below, so the backboard glass is a pale rectangle between them and the viewer. Behind them a sea of yellow: the whole arena is a solid field of yellow light. Black, white and gold on yellow.

the-lob.title: The Lob
the-lob.prompt: The lob, Game 7 of the 2000 Western Conference Finals. Only three figures. A huge centre in a gold jersey with a purple 34 is above the rim with both hands on the ball, catching an alley-oop, about to dunk, mouth open. Below and behind him on the right wing, outside the three-point line, the guard in gold with a purple 8 who threw the pass stands with his right arm still pointed up at the rim. Under the basket a defender in a black jersey is beaten, arms down, turning to watch. The ball's path from the guard's hand to the centre's is a thin gold arc. Everything else is a deep purple void with the key drawn in gold on the floor. Gold and purple on dark purple.

the-last-shot.title: The Last Shot
the-last-shot.look: Classical oil painting, dark and monumental: a vast cathedral nave, one shaft of light from a high window falling on the two men, the hoop hung on a far pillar, a small scoreboard in the dark reading 6.6.
the-last-shot.prompt: Repaint the reference photograph as a classical oil painting, keeping its composition exactly: the same camera position behind the shooter, the same two figures in the same places, the same pose of every limb - the shooter landed with both feet on the floor, right arm forward in the follow-through with the wrist bent down, left arm raised and bent, the defender bent over and stumbling away to the right, the ball in the air above the distant rim, the shot clock above the backboard reading 6.6. Change only the world: the arena becomes a vast dark cathedral nave with one shaft of light from a high window, the crowd becomes shadowed stone arches. The shooter is a Black man in a plain red jersey and shorts with no number and no lettering; the defender wears plain white with purple trim. Faces not visible. No text anywhere except 6.6.
